title: Bioluminescence Imaging for Assessment of Immune Responses Following Implantation of Engineered Heart Tissue (EHT)
protocol: Prepare a master mix containing cells isolated from neonatal ROSA/luciferase-LEW transgenic rat hearts, bovine fibrinogen, and Matrigel.
Create agarose casting molds using Teflon spacers placed in 6-well culture dishes.
Remove Teflon spacers after solidification of the agarose.
Place silicone post racks on culture dishes with posts reaching into the molds.
Mix the master mix briefly with a calculated amount of thrombin.
Pipette the mixture into the mold containing the silicone post racks.
Allow fibrinogen to polymerize, forming EHTs adhering to the posts.
Gently remove silicone racks with EHTs from the agarose casting molds and transfer them to new 6-well cell culture dishes.
Maintain EHTs in a 37°C, 7% CO2 cell culture incubator using custom-made cell culture medium.
Keep EHTs under cell culture conditions until day ten for further development.
Observe spontaneous coherent contractions that deflect silicone posts at the time of implantation.
Anesthetize rats with isoflurane (2.5-3%) using an induction chamber.
Maintain body temperature during the surgical procedure.
Shave the abdominal area of the rat.
Apply eye ointment to prevent drying of the eyes during anesthesia.
Place the rat on its back for surgery.
Disinfect the shaved abdominal area with Betadine and then 80% ethanol, swabbing from clean to dirty.
Check reflexes by pinching the hind feet to ensure sufficient anesthesia.
Drape the animal.
Perform a midline abdominal incision separating the skin and muscle in two steps to open the abdomen.
Use hot bead sterilization between skin and muscle opening.
Place the intestines in a warmed saline moisturized powder-free glove.
Fold the glove around the intestines to prevent loss of moisture.
Remove fatty tissue and expose the spleen.
Visualize and spread the greater omentum with forceps.
Carefully cut EHT from suspending silicone posts.
Transfer EHT onto the greater omentum.
Wrap the greater omentum around the EHT.
Fix using two single 7-0 prolene sutures.
Move the intestines back into the abdomen.
Flush the abdomen with prewarmed sterile saline.
Close the muscle layer of the abdominal wall using 6-0 prolene running sutures.
Use 5-0 prolene running sutures to close the skin.
Inject 5 mg/kg Carprofen subcutaneously while the rat is still in anesthesia.
Anesthetize rat with isoflurane (2.5 - 3%) using an induction chamber.
Disinfect the abdominal and thoracic area widely using Provo-Iodine.
Use 80% ethanol to disinfect the area, repeating three times.
Inject d-Luciferin (Xenogen; 375 mg/kg body weight) i.p.
Place anaesthetized rats into the IVIS imaging chamber.
Assess signal intensity of luc+ cells inside EHT in units of photons/sec/cm2/steradian in the region of interest (ROI).
Create a graph showing the signal intensity over time.
Harvest the spleen of recipient animals 5 days after EHT transplantation.
Isolate recipient splenocytes from the harvested spleens.
Perform Elispot assays using mitomycin-inhibited EHTs as stimulator cells and 5 x10^6 recipient splenocytes as responder cells according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Use IFN-γ coated plates for TH1 response investigation.
Use IL-4 coated plates for TH2 response investigation.
